items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: I always think about what they think — Louis Armstrong and Dizzy, and all those people — they are looking from the sky

ctx.x: I don’t know if you’ll be able to address this or not but do you think that playing with the head more than the soul is partly an outcome of the boom in jazz education?

I’m going to tell you something. We have another problem which is even deeper and more — it’s worse than that. I strongly believe that we have a serious problem, especially in the U.S. with the appreciation and promoting, defending, protecting the immense legacy that we got in our culture about jazz. We don’t feel like that kind of appreciation in general terms. I’m talking about the radio stations, the television, the media in general. We don’t have a little bit of support. I’m going to tell you something. I’m…

It’s a conundrum because you have almost every university in the country now, I don’t know if it’s because it was an artistic decision but more than likely it was a financial decision that having a jazz program was something that they decided to do because they could see that there would be students who would come to their colleges. Yet as you say the respect for the music generally has not kept up with that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
